entries.reason: a class the release does not carry, so the port carries it: MTKModel.h: "Only an MTKMeshBufferAllocator object can initilize a MTKMeshBuffer object" - init is NS_UNAVAILABLE, so the allocator is the only way one is made, and its buffer is "Metal Buffer backing vertex/index data" with an offset that is the "Byte offset of the data within the metal buffer"
entries.effect: a window onto the zone's one MTLBuffer at its own offset and length, carrying the allocator Model I/O needs "for copy and relayout", and answering fillData:offset: and map over the port's CPU-resident bytes

entries.reason: a class the release does not carry, so the port carries it: MTKModel.h: "Initialize the allocator with a device to be used to create buffers" - the designated initializer, and the device is "Device used to create buffers"
entries.effect: the allocator holds the device and every buffer it makes is an MTLBuffer from it, through MDLMeshBufferAllocator's newZone:, newBuffer:type: and newBufferFromZone:length:type:

entries.reason: the zone MTKMeshBufferAllocator hands out: ModelIO's MDLMeshBufferZone is a protocol, and the class that conforms to it is MetalKit's own and is not in the 16.4 headers, so the port defines it wholly (MTKMeshBuffer9.m); the gate found it built with no row
entries.effect: holds the MTLBuffer it was made with, its capacity and how much of it the allocator has handed out, and gives the allocator the buffers it carves from it
entries.source: SDK 16.4, MetalKit and ModelIO: MDLMeshBufferZone's contract (capacity, allocator); the class itself is not declared by any header
